brief:
Israeli occupation authorities have issued new and renewed administrative detention orders against 58 prisoners held across the West Bank, Shehab Wire reported. The detainees come from various areas throughout the occupied territory. Administrative detention is a mechanism that permits Israeli authorities to hold prisoners without bringing formal charges or conducting trial proceedings.

The practice has drawn international criticism for enabling indefinite incarceration. Under Israeli military law, administrative detention orders can be renewed repeatedly, potentially extending confinement for months or years. Human rights organizations have documented the use of administrative detention against Palestinians as a widespread enforcement tool across the West Bank.
